newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica rate hike to dent shares further next week.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica rate hike to dent shares further next week.

text.p: With a month to go until Christmas, South African consumer-based shares will suffer the most next week in the wake of a one point rise in Bank and prime lending rates, which triggered panic selling of stocks.

Hiking rates late Wednesday and opening the game to commercial banks -- which raised prime rates to 20.25 percent -- the Reserve Bank gave the faltering rand a lifeline but pulled the rug out from under equities, portfolio asset managers said.
"The industrial board, particularly the consumer-based shares, will come under further pressure," John Winship, BOE Asset Management managing director, said on Friday.
Industrial shares struggled to find their feet on Friday but are still cowering in the gloom of Thursday's trade which saw their market value cut by 1.2 percent.

"For the man in the street this (rate hike) is the final straw in terms of forcing a cutback in consumption levels. So retail sales and car sales will come under pressure, and those shares will probably see some de-rating," he added.
Denzil Newman, portfolio manager at Syfrets Managed Assets also said the rate hike signalled a de-rating.

"It probably means P/Es (price/earnings ratios) can get down to the 12 to 13 area from the current 15. But you are still getting reasonably good growth from some companies, so prices may be flattish."
Newman added that the rate hike held more sinister implications than just a knock to shares.
"It will knock consumer confidence which means the economy will slow down even more than expected," he said.
Still, with Wall Street robust and the rate hike likely to arrest the rand's decline, no crash was forecast for the stock market next week.
"We don't see a major crash. The market probably has a maximum 10 percent downside," Newman said.
Rand hedge stocks were seen consolidating and shares in niche market companies were expected to rise.
Dealers said that after this week's moderate volumes, trade could pick up next week with most institutions wanting to tidy up their investments ahead of the year-end.
Some dealers and asset managers said that with the rate hike now behind it, the equity market could begin to search elsewhere for direction and the Dow Jones could be chosen as a lead.
"The Dow is looking very healthy. It hasn't set into our market yet because we've had our own problems like an interest rate hike," said Raymond Goss, portfolio manager at Irish & Co.
He added that with the rand looking healthier, overseas investors, previously wary about entering South African investments, could play stocks in greater numbers next week.
"There will be more overseas interest next week because the rand looks to be stabilising and the temptation to come and nibble now will be quite strong," Goss said.

Other guides for South African stocks next week include October trade figures from Monday, third quarter GDP data due at 0900 GMT on Thursday and October money supply numbers expected at 1500 GMT on Friday.
Equity futures contracts were seen consolidating with strengthening predicted for the following week as the mid-December futures close-out nears.
Anglo American Corp of South Africa is due to announce interim results on Tuesday and earnings are seen richer on the back of a robust performance from coal operations.
Amalgamated Banks of South Africa (Absa), posting half year results on Monday, is also seen raising profits, but Sappi Ltd year earnings are expected to plunge.
